flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Flashcards are key to mastering fact-dense UPSC questions. Click on any card below to flip it and reveal the answer.

items.question: What is the ancient Rigvedic name of the River Ravi?
items.answer: Parushni. The Battle of Ten Kings (Dasharajna) was fought on its banks.

items.question: Which river is praised in the Rigveda as 'naditama' (best of all rivers)?
items.answer: Sarasvati. It is described as a mighty flowing river.

items.question: Which mountain peak is mentioned as the source of the Soma plant?
items.answer: Mujavant peak, located in the western Himalayas (Hindukush/Kashmir region).

items.question: How many times is the River Ganga mentioned in the Rigveda?
items.answer: Only once (in the late 10th Mandala - Nadistuti Sukta), showing it lay at the eastern boundary.

items.question: Name the western rivers (in modern Afghanistan) mentioned in the Rigveda.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Master the extent, environmental settings, river nomenclature, and tribal layout of the Rig Vedic period.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
भूगोल

  • सप्त-सिंधु (सात नदियों की भूमि)
  • केंद्र: पंजाब/हरियाणा
  • खानाबदोश पशुपालन चरण

मुख्य विशेषताएं

  • नदी-केंद्रित सभ्यता
  • लोहे का कोई उल्लेख नहीं
  • नदीमाता (नदियों की माता)

भौगोलिक माइंडमैप

  • मुख्य क्षेत्र: सप्त-सिंधु
    • सिंधु - सबसे अधिक बार उल्लिखित
    • सरस्वती - सबसे पवित्र 'नदीतमा'
    • वितस्ता, असिक्नी, परुष्णी, विपाशा, शुतुद्री
  • पर्यावरणीय सीमाएं:
    • उत्तर: हिमालय पर्वत (हिमवत)
    • पश्चिम: अफगानिस्तान/पाकिस्तान सीमा (कुभा नदी का उल्लेख)
    • पूर्व: यमुना/गंगा तक सीमित पहुंच
ऋग्वैदिक नामआधुनिक नाम
सिंधुइंडस
वितस्ताझेलम
असिक्नीचेनाब
परुष्णीरावी
विपाशाब्यास
शुतुद्रीसतलुज

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Rigvedic river systems, consider the following statements:
1. The Nadistuti Sukta lists rivers starting from the west moving towards the east.
2. The River Ganga is mentioned more times than the River Yamuna in the early hymns.
3. The River Sarasvati is praised as the ultimate mother and river ('naditama').
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect (it lists from east to west). Statement 2 is incorrect (Ganga is mentioned only once, Yamuna three times).

practiceQuestions.q: Which mountain range or peak is identified in the Rigveda as the primary source of the Soma plant?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mujavant peak in the Himalayas was the celebrated source of Soma.

practiceQuestions.q: The Battle of Ten Kings (Dasharajna) was fought on the banks of River Parushni. Which modern river corresponds to this name?
practiceQuestions.sol: Parushni is identified with the modern River Ravi.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the geographical location of the Rigvedic river 'Suvastu'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Suvastu corresponds to the modern Swat River, located in northern Pakistan.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigveda, the river 'Vitasta' corresponds to which modern river of the Punjab system?
practiceQuestions.sol: Vitasta is the Rigvedic name for the modern Jhelum River.

practiceQuestions.q: Which modern river corresponds to the Rigvedic name 'Asikni'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Asikni is the Rigvedic name for the Chenab River.

practiceQuestions.q: The modern Sutlej River was known by which ancient name during the Rigvedic period?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sutudri is the ancient Rigvedic name for the modern Sutlej River.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Rigvedic river is identified with the modern Beas River?
practiceQuestions.sol: Vipasa is the Rigvedic name for the Beas River.

practiceQuestions.q: The western Afghan tributary 'Kubha' mentioned in the Rigveda is identified with which modern river?
practiceQuestions.sol: Kubha is identified with the modern Kabul River flowing through Afghanistan and Pakistan.

practiceQuestions.q: Which modern river corresponds to the Rigvedic river name 'Krumu'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Krumu corresponds to the modern Kurram River, a western tributary of the Indus.

practiceQuestions.q: The river 'Gomati' in the western Rigvedic geography represents which modern river?
practiceQuestions.sol: In the western Rigvedic geography, Gomati represents the Gomal River in Baluchistan/Waziristan.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Rigvedic river represents the easternmost boundary of the core Sapta-Sindhu region?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Yamuna river marked the eastern limit of the core Rigvedic settlements.

practiceQuestions.q: The core geographical territory of the Rigvedic people is known in the texts as:
practiceQuestions.sol: Sapta-Sindhu (Land of the Seven Rivers) was the core territory of the early Vedic Aryans.

practiceQuestions.q: The Avestan term 'Hapta-Hendu' corresponds directly to which Sanskrit term?
practiceQuestions.sol: Hapta-Hendu in the Zend Avesta is the Old Iranian equivalent of the Sanskrit Sapta-Sindhu.

practiceQuestions.q: Which geographic term refers to the southern desert margins of the early Vedic world?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dhanva refers to desert zones, particularly the Thar desert margins in the south.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigveda, the Himalayas are celebrated under which of the following names?
practiceQuestions.sol: Himavant is the Rigvedic name for the Himalayan mountain range.

practiceQuestions.q: Which peak of the Himalayas is explicitly mentioned in the Rigveda as the source of the sacred Soma plant?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mujavant peak was renowned in the Rigveda as the place where the best Soma grew.

practiceQuestions.q: The River Sarasvati is praised in the Rigveda with which of the following titles?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sarasvati is praised as 'naditama' (the best of all rivers) and 'ambitama' (the best of all mothers).

practiceQuestions.q: Which river is described as the most important and active economic lifeline ('Hiranyayi') of the Rigvedic people?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indus River (Sindhu) is celebrated for its wealth and called Hiranyayi (golden/rich).

practiceQuestions.q: Which ancient site, often identified with a battle site in the Rigveda, is historically linked to Harappa?
practiceQuestions.sol: Hariyupiya mentioned in Rigveda Mandala VI is identified by some historians with Harappa.

practiceQuestions.q: What geographical boundary did the River Yamuna represent for the early Vedic clans?
opts: The eastern periphery of their expansion
The southern boundary near the Vindhyas
The northern boundary near the Himalayas
practiceQuestions.sol: The Yamuna represented the eastern periphery of the Rigvedic geographical horizon.

practiceQuestions.q: The term 'Samudra' in early Rigvedic hymns is best interpreted as:
opts: A large collection of water or broad river basins
practiceQuestions.sol: In the early Rigveda, 'Samudra' referred to a vast expanse of water or high flood waters, not necessarily the open ocean.

practiceQuestions.q: Which non-Aryan tribe, noted as rich traders, is described as inhabiting the banks of Rigvedic rivers?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Panis were wealthy cattle-owners and traders who lived on the margins of Vedic settlements.

practiceQuestions.q: The geographical term 'Brahmavarta' refers to the land situated between which two rivers?
practiceQuestions.sol: Brahmavarta was the sacred land located between the Sarasvati and Drishadvati rivers.

practiceQuestions.q: The River 'Drishadvati' is identified with which modern river bed?
practiceQuestions.sol: Drishadvati is identified with the modern seasonal Chautang River running parallel to the Sarasvati.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Rigvedic tribe was situated near the confluence of the Vipasa and Sutudri rivers?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Bharatas were situated near the Beas (Vipasa) and Sutlej (Sutudri) river valleys.

practiceQuestions.q: The phonetic shift of 'S' in Sanskrit to 'H' in Old Iranian is demonstrated by which river name pair?
practiceQuestions.sol: All these pairs demonstrate the S-to-H phonetic shift between Indo-Aryan and Iranian languages.

practiceQuestions.q: The river 'Sarasvati' is mentioned in the Zend Avesta as:
practiceQuestions.sol: Sarasvati corresponds to the Avestan Harahvaiti.

practiceQuestions.q: Which river mentioned in the Rigveda is identified with the modern Gomal River?
practiceQuestions.sol: The western Gomal River corresponds to the Rigvedic Gomati.

practiceQuestions.q: How many times is the River Ganga mentioned in the Rigvedic hymns?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Ganga is mentioned only once in the entire Rigveda (in the Nadistuti Sukta).

practiceQuestions.q: The western limit of the early Vedic settlement is represented by rivers flowing in which modern country?
practiceQuestions.sol: Rivers like Kabul (Kubha) and Kurram (Krumu) flow in modern Afghanistan, representing the western limit.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Rigvedic river is identified with the modern Kurram River?
practiceQuestions.sol: Krumu is the Rigvedic name for the Kurram River.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigveda, the River Sarayu corresponds geographically to which area?
opts: The western region (tributary of Indus) or Ayodhya area
practiceQuestions.sol: Sarayu is mentioned in the Rigveda, representing either a western tributary of the Indus or a river in eastern Uttar Pradesh.

practiceQuestions.q: The river 'Arjikiya' mentioned in the Nadistuti Sukta is identified with which modern river?
opts: Haro River or part of Beas
practiceQuestions.sol: Arjikiya is identified with the Haro River in northern Punjab or the upper course of the Beas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Rigvedic river corresponds to the modern Sohan River in Pakistan?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sushoma is the Rigvedic name for the modern Sohan River.

practiceQuestions.q: The river 'Rasa' mentioned in the far western lists of the Rigveda represents which geographical feature?
opts: A mythical river or the Jaxartes/Oxus river
practiceQuestions.sol: Rasa represents either a mythical river surrounding the earth or the Oxus/Jaxartes river in Central Asia.

practiceQuestions.q: The Rigvedic people practiced transhumance. What does this term indicate?
opts: Seasonal migration of pastoralists with their herds between highlands and lowlands
Settled farming in one single plot
practiceQuestions.sol: Transhumance refers to the seasonal movement of people and livestock between summer mountain pastures and winter valleys.

practiceQuestions.q: Which clan fought against the confederacy of ten kings in the Battle of Ten Kings?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Bharatas (led by King Sudas of the Tritsu clan) fought against the confederacy of ten kings.

practiceQuestions.q: The Vindhya mountains were first mentioned and explored during which Vedic phase?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vindhyas were outside the early Rigvedic geographical limit and were only named in Later Vedic literature.

practiceQuestions.q: The Rigveda mentions the Gandharis in connection with which economic product of their region?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Gandharis are mentioned for their excellent wool-producing sheep in the northwest.

practiceQuestions.q: The tree 'Asvattha' (Pipal) mentioned in the Rigveda is geographically native to which zone?
practiceQuestions.sol: Asvattha (Ficus religiosa) is native to the plains and foothills of northern India.

practiceQuestions.q: The climate of the Sapta-Sindhu region during the early Vedic period was generally:
opts: Semi-arid to temperate with wet summers
practiceQuestions.sol: The climate was semi-arid to temperate grasslands fed by massive river networks.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Rigvedic term refers to the paths or routes constructed for caravans and chariots?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pathya refers to the established pathways or routes used for migration and trade.

practiceQuestions.q: The deified term 'Aranyani' in the Rigveda represents which geographic feature?
practiceQuestions.sol: Aranyani is celebrated in Rigveda Mandala X as the goddess of forests and wilderness.

practiceQuestions.q: The easternmost expansion of the Vedic tribes before the PGW phase was stopped by which barrier?
opts: Dense forests of the Gangetic valley
practiceQuestions.sol: The dense monsoon-fed forests of the Gangetic valley blocked easy clearance before the use of iron technology.

practiceQuestions.q: The name 'Hariyupiya' is mentioned in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
practiceQuestions.sol: Hariyupiya is mentioned in Mandala VI of the Rigveda.

practiceQuestions.q: Which river mentioned in the Rigveda is located in modern western Uttar Pradesh?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Yamuna river flows through western Uttar Pradesh, marking the eastern boundary of the early Vedic world.

practiceQuestions.q: The Indus river is described in the Rigveda as having how many outlets or stages?
opts: Multiple channels leading to the samudra
A single straight path into a lake
Disappearing in the sands of Thar
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indus is described as flowing actively with multiple channels towards the samudra (large water collection/delta).

practiceQuestions.q: The Sanskrit word 'Giri' is used in the Rigveda to denote:
practiceQuestions.sol: Giri is the standard Rigvedic term for mountains or hills.

practiceQuestions.q: Which tribal groups participated in the Battle of Ten Kings against King Sudas?
opts: Purus, Yadus, Turvasas, Anus, Druhyus and non-Aryan clans
practiceQuestions.sol: The confederacy consisted of five major Aryan clans (Purus, Yadus, Turvasas, Anus, Druhyus) along with five minor non-Aryan clans.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which modern geographic region represents the core area of the Rigvedic 'Sapta-Sindhu'?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Sapta-Sindhu heartland corresponds to Punjab, Haryana, and eastern parts of Pakistan.

mockTestQuestions.q: The Avestan term 'Hapta-Hendu' matches the Sanskrit 'Sapta-Sindhu'. This represents which linguistic rule?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The S-to-H phonetic shift is characteristic of Old Iranian languages compared to Indo-Aryan.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which river is described as the easternmost limit in the Rigvedic Nadistuti Sukta?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Nadistuti Sukta lists rivers from east to west, starting with the Ganga.

mockTestQuestions.q: The western tributaries of the Indus River mentioned in the Rigveda are geographically located in:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Kubha (Kabul) and Krumu (Kurram) flow through eastern Afghanistan.

mockTestQuestions.q: The Rigvedic term 'Dhanva' refers to which type of geographic feature?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Dhanva refers to desert zones, particularly the Thar desert margins.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which Rigvedic river is identified with the modern Chenab River?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Asikni is the ancient name of the Chenab.

mockTestQuestions.q: The Rigvedic people referred to the Himalayas as:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Himavant was the name used for the Himalayas in the hymns.

mockTestQuestions.q: How many times is the River Yamuna mentioned in the Rigveda?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Yamuna is mentioned three times, showing it was at the edge of their territory.

mockTestQuestions.q: The paleochannels of which river system are linked to the Rigvedic Sarasvati?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Ghaggar-Hakra paleochannels correspond closely to the Sarasvati.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which Vedic tribe was situated closest to the Yamuna river boundary?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Bharatas were located at the eastern edge near the Yamuna boundary.
